text.p: Primus Telecommunications Group Inc said Thursday it contines to expect a net loss for 1997 of $0.90 to $1.00 a share.
The company said costs in the first quarter will increase by $700,000 to $800,000, with no offsetting revenue rise, as a result of what Primus alleged was fraud by one of its customers.
The company alleged that the customer failed to pay it after falsifying credit reports and other documentation.
Because Primus acted as a reseller in the incident, it said it was obligated to pay the underlying carrier for the service provided.
It said it is instituting various measures to monitor off-network customer usage and unusual activity more closely.
Primus provides domestic and international long-distance switched voice, data, private network and other telecommunications services.
